rationale: The answer covers most of the central content without inventing a vendor quote or dollar range. One-time costs include legal/registration, index setup, listing/platform onboarding and launch marketing. Recurring costs include index, admin, custody, transfer agency, audit, board, listing/data and platform distribution, with sponsor absorption above the unitary cap. It correctly treats seed as a sponsor investment, not an expense, and gives break-even as F/(f−v), matching the key formula. Omissions and localized errors: (1) It never notes the Investment Company Act §14(a) $100,000 net-worth condition as the regulatory seed baseline, distinct from launch cost or commercial break-even. (2) It presents payer allocations as fixed rules ('sponsor-paid', 'typically sponsor-borne') rather than contractual terms that vary by agreement. The Lazard example of the manager bearing organization costs without recoupment and paying trustees directly is not reflected. (3) On break-even it does not say the formula holds only when f−v > 0. It instead writes 'retained margin is positive only above that level', which confuses fund-level profitability above break-even AUM with the per-unit margin condition the question asks about. (4) Saying seed 'is recovered as shares are sold and redeemed' overstates certainty, since seed is exposed to market loss. Useful and largely sound, but these gaps on the positive-margin condition and contractual allocation are substantive.
